articles.title: Mustard, golf balls and a playoff bid: Lane Kiffin's return to Tennessee has it all
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin once again knows LSU is about to walk into a 'toxic' environment at Neyland Stadium.
articles.body:
The SEC schedule is a three-month-long family reunion of a particularly fractious family. Everybody's got history with everybody else, meaning every Saturday is a stew of seething resentments and subtle below-the-surface slights. In other words: Get those golf balls and mustard bottles ready, Lane Kiffin's coming back to Tennessee.

Kiffin's LSU Tigers visit Neyland Stadium to face the Volunteers on Saturday afternoon, and the storylines abound. First and foremost, this is Tennessee's chance to bolster — or torpedo — its College Football Playoff bid. The Vols currently sit 9th in the rankings, but the CFP committee hasn't held out much love for Tennessee despite its victory over No. 3 Alabama. Another loss will make 8-2 Tennessee's return to the playoffs — the Vols were in the initial 12-team field two years ago — that much tougher.

LSU, meanwhile, saw its CFP hopes evaporate with one swing pass last week against Texas. Needing big wins over both Texas and Tennessee, the highly touted, highly paid Tigers faltered, and they've since dropped out of the rankings entirely.

That loss to Texas deflates the value of this game from a CFP standpoint, but in terms of pure meanness, well, the stakes are as high as ever. After all, if you can't make the playoff yourself, why not drag someone into the pit with you?

Schematically, this is going to be a battle of defenses, since the offenses can't seem to do anything right, well or consistently through the air. Tennessee's passing game ranks 123rd in the country, with George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon combining for only 171.5 yards per game and just 11 touchdowns. Running back DeSean Bishop leads the SEC with 1,163 yards rushing, and leads the entire country with 230 carries, which should give you an idea of how Tennessee balances its offense.

LSU, meanwhile, will throw Sam Leavitt back into the meat grinder for (perhaps) one of the last times. Leavitt has thrown for 280 yards a game, but it's the completions to the other team that have been the problem; his 12 interceptions have annihilated the Tigers in game after game, and nobody in the LSU stands seems particularly devoted to defending him right now.

So Saturday will rest on the defenses — Tennessee's Jim Knowles-led beast and LSU's smothering monster. Both are among the national leaders in sacks, yards allowed and other fearsome stats, and both have meaty opportunities in front of them on Saturday.

"Obviously, another big football game against a really good opponent," Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel said earlier this week. "They've lost some close football games, but they're a talented roster, good coaches. Huge test, huge opportunity this Saturday."

As for Kiffin — well, at this point you need a decent memory to recall exactly why he and Tennessee have beef; Kiffin has burnt bridges at four schools since his one year in Knoxville. Back in 2009, the then-33-year-old wonderkid showed up in Knoxville as the forward-looking sequel to the recently fired Philip Fulmer … and lasted for all of one 7-6 season before bouncing for the USC job. Students then at UT — some of whom are now approaching 40 — railed at Kiffin for leaving, painting The Rock on campus with NSFW farewell messages .

When Kiffin, then the coach of Ole Miss, returned to Neyland Stadium in 2021 and posted a 31-26 victory, students rained down mustard bottles, beer cans and hot dogs on the assembled Rebels, and Kiffin himself brandished a golf ball that had come from the stands. Ole Miss left with the win, Tennessee had to apologize for the late-game hailstorm, and a meme was born.

Heupel has leaned into the mess. "I certainly hope our fan base hasn't cooled off," he said this past summer at SEC media days . "Whether it's the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard, or our sports stores making sure that they've got reinforcements on the golf balls, hopefully Knoxville is ready for his arrival."

"They have done a great job creating a home-field advantage. They've always had a great one," Kiffin said earlier this week . "I feel like we've been in so many toxic environments and things so far, that it'll just be more of it. I really hadn't thought much about it." (One could note that if you're entering into toxic environment after toxic environment, that might say as much about you as the environment, but at this point in LSU's season, that just feels like piling on.)

Since the programs were formerly seated in different divisions, the Tigers and Vols haven't played each other frequently as of late. Tennessee won their most recent matchup, in Baton Rouge in 2022, snapping a five-game LSU win streak that dated to 2006. Tennessee hasn't beaten LSU in Knoxville since 2001, long before most of the students who will show up Saturday were even born.

LSU-Tennessee kicks off at 3:30 Eastern under what's likely to be a beautiful blue Knoxville sky. Sure, the game isn't all it could be from a CFP perspective, but as long as Lane Kiffin is involved, there's always going to be a little mustard on it.

articles.title: Mykhailo Mudryk accuses Andriy Shevchenko of lying about drugs test claims
articles.summary: Mykhailo Mudryk accuses Ukraine legend Andriy Shevchenko of lying about the circumstances surrounding the winger's positive drugs test as his dispute with the country's football federation continues.
articles.body:
Mykhailo Mudryk has accused Ukraine legend Andriy Shevchenko of lying about the circumstances surrounding the winger's positive drugs test as his dispute with the country's football federation continues.

Tottenham Hotspur winger Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan from Chelsea , was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium.

In an interview on Wednesday, Mudryk said he blames the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban, believing it entered his system while on international duty.

In response , Shevchenko, the UAF president, accused Mudryk's representatives of repeatedly asking for a UAF employee to "falsely" take the blame for his failed test.

Former Chelsea and AC Milan striker Shevchenko also said Mudryk's comments amounted to a "baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally", and called on the player to retract his words.

In a statement on Friday, Mudryk refuted Shevchenko's accusation, saying it was a "lie" and that "neither I nor my representatives made any such request".

Mudryk has also accused the UAF of attempting to mislead his team's investigation into the reasons behind his failed test, and claims to have evidence proving it.

"My team and I repeatedly asked the UAF to help establish how I might have been exposed to meldonium and who, if anyone, might have been responsible," said Mudryk.

"In several letters to the UAF at the time, my lawyers made clear that we were seeking truthful information that could be independently verified. One of those letters was leaked to the media by the UAF earlier today and clearly shows that my lawyers wanted 'true, verifiable and reliable information'.

"Further, the UAF were repeatedly unhelpful and even attempted to mislead my team in order to distance themselves from the case. For example, UAF staff testified at my hearing that I was not using the UAF's supplements and Mr Shevchenko has repeated that assertion in his statement - but I have WhatsApp messages that prove that I was using their products during their training camps. That is, I have evidence to prove that their repeated assertions are wrong."

Mudryk also said the UAF was "repeatedly slow" to respond to requests from his team and "withheld important information and documents" from his lawyers.

BBC Sport has contacted the UAF for comment.

articles.title: El Espanyol coge gusto a San Mamés
articles.standfirst: Los de Sarabia repiten la victoria que lograron un año atrás con Manolo González
articles.summary: Los de Sarabia repiten la victoria que lograron un año atrás con Manolo González
articles.body: El Espanyol va a pedir jugar más de una vez por temporada en San Mamés. Ganó el pasado año remontando a un Athletic que acostumbraba a no ceder cuando se ponía por delante en el marcador y ha repetido este viernes en el primer partido de Eder Sarabia en el banquillo, pues los dos anteriores de su recién iniciada etapa como perico tuvo que verlos desde la grada por la sanción federativa que arrastraba de su última estancia en el Elche. Así que el Espanyol se mantiene invicto con Sarabia y el Athletic vuelve a sentir lo que es salir derrotado en su campo después de cinco encuentros consecutivos sin hacerlo. El conjunto catalán se estira y tomará el partido del viernes siguiente en Vitoria como la puerta a otros objetivos mientras que al Athletic se le cruza ahora la obligatoriedad de ganar al Málaga -equipo que todavía no conoce la victoria- para no pinchar el globo de ilusión por alcanzar la Navidad en posiciones europeas. Los defensores de que los buenos principios no son reflejo de nada más que un buen principio habrán firmado con sangre lo vivido en San Mamés. El Athletic arrancó veloz y vertical frente a un Espanyol demasiado lagunero en defensa. Parecía el inicio de una noche redonda para los de Terzic, pero los leones dejaron claro que lo suyo no es la finura ofensiva y el Espanyol, que tampoco la tuvo, cambió de registro para tirar rápido hacia la portería de Simón. El Espanyol tardó en ajustar la presión, aunque el Athletic fracasó en su intento de poner en aprietos a Fortuño porque sus futbolistas se enredaban cuando el balón rondaba la zona de remate. La ocasión más clara de los leones en la primera mitad fue de Iñaki Williams en el minuto 32...Remató mal un buen centro de Nico y el portero perico desvió a córner. A esas alturas de encuentro Simón había tenido que lucir guantes de oro ante Pere Milla (13’) y Roberto (19’). Hubo más, porque su mejor parada de ese periodo se dio en el minuto 36, cuando fue rápido al suelo para desviar un disparo cruzado de Alex Santiago en una rápida contra del Espanyol. La espesura continuó en una segunda mitad en la que el Athletic repitió todos sus problemas porque el paso por vestuarios no provocó cambio alguno. Los nubarrones rojiblancos no fueron acicate para que el Espanyol afilara colmillo. Así que la posibilidad de que el empate no fuera eterno quedó para una genialidad. La firmó Roberto, pasada la hora de partido, definiendo como se espera tras llegar al área en velocidad. La tabla del balancín podía haberse ido poco antes hacia el otro lado porque Nico también tuvo la suya, pero eligió un remate que sólo se da en las consolas de play station. Igual le fue a su hermano Iñaki cuando en el minuto 76 no le dio para llegar a un balón al espacio que terminó ganándole Fortuño.

articles.title: Barnsley 1-2 Sheffield Wednesday
articles.summary: A rapid-fire Jamal Lowe double set Sheffield Wednesday up for a 2-1 win at neighbours Barnsley.
articles.body:
Sloppy defending from the hosts cost them on a night where fans protested against the club's ownership as their winless streak extended to 10 league games.

Wednesday went in front with their first attack of the game on nine minutes when Liam Cooper headed Barry Bannan's free-kick back across goal and Lowe slotted home.

Lowe doubled the tally on 14 minutes in easy fashion when he was found by Bannan and then drove into the bottom corner from the edge of the box.

Barnsley got back into it on 40 minutes when Reyes Cleary's cross from the left was forced in by Vimal Yoganathan.

Lowe came within inches of getting his hat-trick when his chipped effort just had too much on it after Cieran Slicker had raced out of his goal.

Barnsley remained bright in the second half but the better chances were falling the way of the visitors with Bannan and Davis Keillor-Dunn having efforts blocked.

Luca Connell's late free-kick had to be tipped over by Wednesday keeper Joe Lumley.

articles.title: Coventry: Frank Lampard fumes and calls for fairness after Sky Blues penalty woe
articles.summary: Coventry boss Frank Lampard wants officials to spend time ensuring they get decisions correct in the wake of his side being denied a penalty at Everton.
articles.body:
Frustrated Frank Lampard has called for fairness from officials after Coventry were denied a clear penalty - with the boss claiming it got less coverage because they are a smaller club.

The Sky Blues were furious they were not awarded a first-half spot kick in the 3-1 defeat at Everton before the international break.

James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair in the area but was not penalised by referee Stuart Attwell or video assistant referee (VAR) Timothy Wood.

The Key Match Incidents Panel, which assesses the contentious incidents and whether the officials got them correct, this week voted unanimously that the Sky Blues should have been awarded a penalty.

It would have given Coventry a chance to go 1-0 up, before Yann Gboho fired them ahead early in the second half - only for Everton to recover.

Thierno Barry scored twice, and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added the third for the hosts but Lampard also argued because the decisions went against Coventry they were not given the same scrutiny as others.

"I'm not sure how much coverage it got in the days after, maybe because we're Coventry , move on everybody," said Lampard, with defeat leaving them 17th in the Premier League.

"We lost a game and we move on but we need fairness.

"If the decision is rightly for us give it to us, I'm not asking for anything beyond that.

"We're not asking for anything beyond fairness to get the right decision, to spend enough time on the decision. We're fighting on so many levels here as a promoted club.

"We've been out of the league for 25 years, we've got a lack of experience in the squad because the boys that have come up haven't played in the Premier League.

"Financially what we do in the league, in terms of where we are and the wages, we know we're right at the bottom and all these things, so we're fighting for every moment and we're grafting a lot and you just really do want that fairness."

Coventry also felt they could have had a penalty when Taiwo Awoniyi was tripped by Vitalii Mykolenko early in the second half and that Everton striker Thierno Barry handled the ball before scoring his crucial second goal.

Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb has spoken with Lampard and Coventry sporting director Dean Austin over the decisions, with Webb acknowledging the wrong decision over the hair pull.

The hair pulling guidance was relaxed in the summer with referees advised it would not necessarily mean a straight red card, although sources accept the softening of guidance could lead to more grey areas at times - something Lampard disputed in this instance.

"There was no grey area with this, they missed it. They watched the video and they missed it," said Lampard, before Saturday's visit of Crystal Palace .

"They watched it for a good minute and a half. I've seen it and I've heard the footage. They missed it completely.

"I got fined once for talking about a referee as manager of Everton and I hate talking about it but when you work for the club you feel the pain yourself.

"You fight all week for a result and there's something with real clarity that can't really be missed. The Tarkowski one, it can't be missed at this level.

"So that's quite hard to take as well because we all saw it on the Sky broadcast pretty much straight away. So I respect and appreciate Howard Webb saying that to myself and Dean in a meeting afterwards.

"I like that side of things. Howard Webb was, when I was playing, one of the best referees in the world and I think he's very good at his job. He was upfront about the fact they missed it."

articles.title: Un doblete de Flakus rompe la racha del Castilla
articles.standfirst: El filial blanco cae derrotado por el Murcia en el Di Stéfano, donde venía sumando desde finales de septiembre
articles.summary: El filial blanco cae derrotado por el Murcia en el Di Stéfano, donde venía sumando desde finales de septiembre
articles.body: Con Pedro León en el palco del Di Stéfano, esta vez como presidente del Real Murcia, el Castilla cayó derrotado con contundencia ante la atenta mirada de Mourinho, sentado a pocos metros del que fuera su jugador en 2010. El Murcia, mediante el doblete del esloveno Flakus, infligió un duro castigo de juego y resultado en la primera mitad a los pupilos blancos, del que no supieron reponerse los locales. Los de López de Lerma se vieron rebasados en una primera parte en la que el resultado ponía justicia a lo visto sobre el terreno del Di Stéfano. Superados en la medular y avasallados en las internadas por el costado diestro, el filial blanco vivió una primera parte para olvidar en la que apenas contó con algún arreón reseñable tras el primer tanto de Flakus asistido por Javi Moreno en el 26’. Carvajal en un remate sin oposición ante la meta pimentonera pudo haber empatado, pero el momento blanco se diluyó de nuevo con la contundencia murciana. Jorge Mier aprovechó las pocas ayudas a Diego Aguado para internarse por su banda y tras pase a Palmberg, llegó el fortísimo chut de Flakus en el que Mestre no pudo hacer más por evitar el gol. Sí lo hizo para evitar el que hubiera sido el tercero poco antes del descanso a remate de Jorge Mier. Con la entrada de Ciria tras el descanso, el filial madridista intentaba provocar alguna acción que les abriera la puerta a la remontada, aunque el Murcia mostró su personalidad a la hora de cerrar filas y evitar riesgos innecesarios. El equipo de Sergi Guilló tuvo el choque bajo su mano en todo momento y no dudó en seguir percutiendo en busca de aumentar la ventaja. El filial blanco apenas gozó de remates testimoniales, destacando el de Roberto Martín desde fuera del área o el de Mesonero en su internada en el área a pocos minutos para el final del tiempo reglamentario. El Castilla no supo encontrar el punto débil de un Murcia con hechuras de equipo que presenta candidatura al ascenso. articles.title: Harry Kane: England and Bayern Munich striker set to miss three months with ankle injury
articles.summary: Harry Kane was withdrawn after 20 minutes of Bayern's Bundesliga game against Cologne; the injury comes days after the England captain became his country's most-capped player; Kane won the Ballon d'Or earlier this month; Michael Olise also taken off injured in 1-1 draw
articles.body:
Sky Germany report Bayern sporting director Max Eberl confirmed shortly after the 1-1 draw that Kane had suffered a "syndesmosis ligament tear" - also known as a high ankle sprain.

The Ballon d'Or winner - who became England's most-capped player last week - was seeking a first goal in five matches for the Bundesliga leaders.

However, as he looked to latch on to Michael Olise's deflected low cross at the back post, Cologne full-back Joel Schmied got to the ball first and clattered into Kane's left leg in his follow through.

Kane immediately clutched his lower leg and writhed in pain for a few moments before gingerly getting back to his feet, but he was a virtual bystander for the next couple of minutes.

The 33-year-old gestured to the dugout, sunk to the turf and then received treatment on his ankle before making way for Tom Bischof, limping off the field alongside two physios.

Kane had a quick exchange with Vincent Kompany, who was back in the Bayern hot-seat for the first time in six matches after being diagnosed with meningeal irritation last month, before heading down the tunnel.

To make matters worse for Bayern, Olise was also taken off injured at half-time.

A three-month period on the sidelines would rule Kane out for 11 Bundesliga games, the DFB-Pokal round of 16 tie against Hertha Berlin, as well as all four of Bayern's remaining Champions League league phase matches.

Providing his recovery goes to plan, that would give the striker just over a month to prepare for England's Nations League quarter-final.

The Three Lions face Norway in Oslo in the first leg on March 27, before the return leg at Wembley on March 30.

Henry Winter speaking on Back Pages Tonight:

"I've covered Harry Kane's career for so many years and there was a period where he had almost a chronic problem with his ankles.

"It's three months and, most immediately, it's Bayern Munich's concern. But England have the home and away Nations League quarter-finals against Norway in late March.

"The timeline would suggest he'll be back in that time, but thoughts with Thomas Tuchel tonight because he'll be absolutely concerned about this.

"He's such an important player. England's No 9. There's a bit of a gap behind him if you're looking for No 9s. I know Jude Bellingham can play there and that's probably the long-term plan. But this is hugely alarming."

articles.title: Tom Brady: NFL great could buy Chelsea stake
articles.summary: American football great Tom Brady is looking to invest in Chelsea through ownership group Clearlake Capital.
articles.body:
American football great Tom Brady is looking to invest in Chelsea through ownership group Clearlake Capital.

The seven-time Super Bowl winner has recently divested his stake in Championship club Birmingham City, which he bought into following Tom Wagner's Knighthead Capital takeover in 2023.

It now appears he could move into Chelsea , where he has a positive relationship with influential co-owner Behdad Eghbali, having been a star guest at the after-party following the club's Club World Cup triumph in 2025.

Brady would have no voting rights or control at Chelsea , although the ownership group could look to appoint him to the board if it suited all parties.

The move is not said to be linked to Todd Boehly and Mark Walter's £950m sale of their stakes to Clearlake Capital, which must be completed by the end of the year.

Meanwhile, Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss remains a significant minority stakeholder at Stamford Bridge.

The investment is also not part of a funding round, according to senior sources, and is not intended to dilute Clearlake Capital's control.

However, other interested parties are said to have approached them about investing since Boehly and Walter agreed a deal to leave.

Former quarterback Brady, a three-time NFL most valuable player, retired in February 2023 after 23 seasons in the NFL, having won six Super Bowl rings with the New England Patriots and one with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Following the end of his playing career he acquired a stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, while also becoming part of the ownership group of the WNBA's Las Vegas Aces.

On top of that, Brady's commitments include him being a lead NFL analyst for Fox Sports.

articles.title: Florentino Pérez presenta cuentas históricas y un galáctico
articles.standfirst: El Real Madrid celebra su Asamblea con récord de ingresos y con el fichaje de la leyenda del tenis para dar más solidez al proyecto
articles.summary: El Real Madrid celebra su Asamblea con récord de ingresos y con el fichaje de la leyenda del tenis para dar más solidez al proyecto
articles.body: El Real Madrid celebra mañana su Asamblea de Socios Compromisarios en la que se van a aprobar las cuentas de la campaña pasada y el presupuesto de este ejercicio. Un año más, al club blanco le cuadran los números y eso que este año el gasto ha aumentado con los fichajes (el gasto salarial y de amortizaciones de las plantillas deportivas representó el 46 % sobre los ingresos, subiendo 3 puntos respecto al 43 % del curso anterior), pero la novedad estará en el punto extraordinario en el orden del día con la votación para incorporar a Rafa Nadal como nuevo miembro de la Junta Directiva. La cita en la que Florentino Pérez rinde cuentas no puede llegar en mejor momento, sobre todo si echan la vista atrás, hace apenas mes y medio, con un Madrid de Mou plagado de dudas y tras dos años sin títulos. Pero la racha de ocho triunfos seguidos y lo que transmite al equipo han cambiado radicalmente la tendencia. En lo económico, los socios votan el cierre récord del ejercicio 2025/2026 (1.221,3 millones de euros de ingresos) y un presupuesto histórico de unos 1.400 millones de euros para la temporada 2026/2027. 1.221,3 millones de euros (un 3,1 % más que la temporada anterior y sin contar plusvalías por traspasos). El estadio Santiago Bernabéu duplicó sus ingresos respecto a antes de la reforma (+107 %), situándose en unos 363 millones de euros. El resultado después de impuestos fue de 26,3 millones de euros. El golpe maestro de Florentino se va a confirmar también hoy cuando los socios compromisarios voten de forma unánime por la incorporación de Rafa Nadal a la junta directiva. Es una maniobra de impacto a corto plazo porque el madridismo tiene al ex tenista en un pedestal. Su llegada a nivel de imagen ya se va a notar y luego habrá que ver los efectos a medio y largo plazo: su papel estos años y si apunta a asumir el relevo del actual presidente, que al fin y al cabo asume con esta decisión que todo se acaba aunque sea como ley de vida. El discurso de Florentino fue subiendo de tono con el paso de los años hasta alcanzar la cima el año pasado, una vez que el Barça dejó de ser aliado al abandonar la Superliga. Sin embargo, para este año las palabras del presidente puede que encuentren menos enemigos. Con UEFA ya llueve menos, por lo que Aleksander Ceferin no debería estar en la lista, al igual que Nasser al Khelaifi, que ya ha destacado el papel crucial de Florentino en el fútbol español y que está a la espera de que se fomalice su regreso de forma oficial a la EFC (la asociación de clubes europeos) que él preside. Sin embargo, no sería extraño que Javier Tebas, presidente de la Liga, y Joan Laporta por el caso Negreira, tengan mención en el discurso del presidente.

articles.title: Duncan Ferguson: First defeat and first red for Scotsman as Glentoran falter
articles.summary: BBC Sport Northern Ireland looks at Duncan Ferguson's first red card and defeat as Glentoran manager as they are edged out 3-2 by Cliftonville on Friday.
articles.body:
It was a night of unfortunate firsts for Duncan Ferguson at Solitude on Friday.

The Everton great suffered his first defeat as Glentoran boss as they were edged out 3-2 by Cliftonville in an Irish Premiership thriller.

He also received his first red card as a manager, after picking up nine during his playing career, in the first half for protesting the decision to award Cliftonville's first goal after he perceived a foul in the build-up.

The defeat ended Glentoran's eight-game unbeaten run in the league and leaves them well off the pace in pursuit of their first league title since 2009.

While he has delivered with his animated touchline antics, Ferguson has so far struggled to get much out of his side on the pitch.

Ferguson sent off as Reds beat Glens in thriller - report and highlights

'The manager got frustrated because it was a foul'

The Glens were second best for much of the first half in north Belfast, with Cliftonville dominating possession and creating the better chances.

Still, the awarding of the Reds' first goal was controversial as it looked like defender Jarlath O'Rourke had been pushed by Liam McStravick, who then teed up Joe Sheridan to score the opener on 38 minutes.

Ferguson was incensed that the goal stood, protesting while his side went up the other end and scored an equaliser through Cal Weatherup's deflected strike a minute later.

Such was the vehemence of his words towards the officials, referee Ben McMaster brandished a straight red card and Ferguson was forced to make the long walk to the tunnel all while being jeered by Cliftonville supporters.

"I think the manager got frustrated because it was a foul. It changes the dynamic [the sending off], he's a leader, I've then got to step in and fill his boots and it's a big set of boots to fill," said Ferguson's assistant Gary Bollan.

His side looked to have received a stern talking to from Bollan at half-time as they were much more competitive after the break.

They responded to Brian Healy putting the Reds ahead once again with a fine James Douglas strike on 86 minutes, which looked to be enough to secure a point and continue their unbeaten run.

However, they failed to stop midfielder Sheridan, who waltzed into the box before firing into the top corner two minutes later to seal a win.

Glentoran's fifth league defeat of the campaign leaves them 14 points behind pacesetters Linfield.

Former Crusaders captain Colin Coates, who was on co-commentary duties for the game for BBC Sport NI, believes Ferguson and the club have "a lot of work to do" to get back challenging for major honours.

"Look at the squad, there is work to do in January and next summer," he added.

"Duncan Ferguson will use this next few months to assess what he has, what he wants to keep and what he needs to bring in to make them competitive. Every time I watch them I want more from them.

"There is a real lack of quality particularly at the top end they don't look like they can hurt teams aside from Jordan Stewart. A lot of work and soul searching to do and players will be playing for their futures."

Stewart was suspended for the game at Solitude and was a big miss while Ferguson will hope to get more out of Conor McMenamin and the fit-again Pat Hoban, who both came on in the second half.

The Glens face two games against Larne, one in the BetMcLean Cup on Tuesday and one in the league next Friday and Ferguson will hope to mastermind two big results to really kick-start his reign.

For Cliftonville, it was a case of another big performance under the lights on a Friday in front of a raucous Solitude crowd.

The Reds beat Larne 4-2 at the same venue a fortnight ago and key in their two big wins in recent weeks has been teenage midfielder Sheridan, who is growing in stature for Jim Magilton.

The 19-year-old broke into the senior squad last season after a fruitful six-month spell at Queen's University in the 2024-25 campaign.

He won the club's Young Player of the Year award last season and was a rotation option, but he has kicked on again this year and firmly established himself in a midfield three with captain Rory Hale and Dean McMaster.

The next step for the talented Northern Ireland under-21 international is adding goals and assists to his game and he certainly delivered on Friday.

Former Glentoran captain Paul Leeman said he showed "composure" for both his goals, first to curl home from close range, then to weave his way into the box and place the ball in the top corner.

"It was a really good performance from him. He's becoming a mainstay in the team," Leeman added.

The victory moves Cliftonville to within a point of the Glens and with games against struggling Ballymena United and Bangor to come, they will hope to embark upon another winning run to continue their surge up the table.

articles.title: Manchester United: Cost of hiring and firing managers nears £100m
articles.summary: Manchester United borrowed £10m three days after confirming Mauricio Pochettino would be their new head coach, which will cost them £7.5m in compensation to US Soccer.
articles.body:
Manchester United borrowed another £10m three days after confirming Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach.

In an extended Stock Market filing to go with their first-quarter financial results that were released on Thursday, United said they would be liable to pay £7.5m in compensation to US Soccer to hire the Argentine.

United announced Pochettino had agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal on 13 November. They borrowed £10m on 16 November.

The loan is one of three confirmed after the 30 September first-quarter reporting date, which takes the overall amount owed on their rolling credit limit to £240m.

The amount paid to release Pochettino from his USA deal takes the sums paid hiring and firing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 to £95m. However, that figure is likely to top £100m once the cost of hiring Pochettino's staff and sacking Michael Carrick is added.

Carrick was sacked last week with the club in the relegation zone and enduring their worst start to a season in 40 years. The former midfielder only signed a two-year contract in the summer after a successful six-month spell in caretaker charge last season.

Pochettino is the ninth full-time manager to be appointed since Ferguson, including Ralf Rangnick in November 2021. United have changed their manager in the middle of the last three campaigns.

The club also confirmed they had spent £5.7m to either acquire or extend registrations of "certain players and members of coaching staff".

The filing also revealed they owe £417m in outstanding transfer fees, £181m of which is due after one year. United said on Thursday their substantial $750m debt was £577.4m when converted to sterling on 30 September.

articles.title: Bayern Munich star Harry Kane expected to miss multiple months with ligament tear
articles.summary: The reigning Ballon d'Or winner sustained the tear during a home match on Friday.
articles.body:
Harry Kane will be out for the near future. Bayern Munich announced Friday that the star forward has suffered a torn ligament in his left ankle. He will miss multiple months while recovering.

Kane sustained the tear to the syndesmosis ligament of his left ankle on Friday, early in Bayern's home match against FC Köln. Kane had to be subbed out in the 20th minute of the 1-1 draw, though he was able to walk off the field under his own power.

Kane underwent medical testing after the game that confirmed the tear, per the club.

With Bayern Munich less than a third of the way through the season, Kane has four goals and eight assists, which leads the team.

Kane, 33, is also just a few weeks removed from winning his first Ballon d'Or , beating out La Liga stars Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal for the honor. Kane was emotional after earning the award, calling Bayern Munich "an honor to play for."

Earlier this month, Kane signed an extension to stay with Bayern through 2029. The deal reportedly earns the striker $28 million per year, which makes him the highest-paid player in Europe.

Kane's Ballon d'Or win came off a monster 2025-26 season with Bayern Munich, during which he scored 61 goals across all competitions for Bayern, including 36 goals in 31 Bundesliga games — making him the top scorer internationally. He also captained England to its best World Cup finish in six decades this summer.

articles.title: "Doctors started prescribing her sedatives": Cristiano Ronaldo's rise to football stardom came with a heartbreaking cost for his mother
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo had spent his career performing in front of millions, handling enormous pressure and delivering on football's biggest stages.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo had spent his career performing in front of millions, handling enormous pressure and delivering on football's biggest stages. But his early professional years had brought a different kind of pressure to his family. His mother, Maria Dolores, found it so difficult to watch him play that she fainted during matches. The Portuguese superstar shared this deeply personal memory in a letter published by The Players' Tribune on October 2, 2017. Looking back at his journey, Ronaldo revealed how his rise in football had affected the woman who had supported him long before the world knew his name.Cristiano Ronaldo revealed why his mother fainted during his matchesRonaldo was only 17 when he began playing professional football. His career was just getting started, but the excitement of watching her son compete soon became overwhelming for Maria Dolores.She regularly attended his games at the old Estádio José Alvalade, where he played for Sporting Lisbon. However, the tension of important matches became too much for her. Ronaldo recalled that her nervousness sometimes caused her to lose consciousness in the stadium.In his October 2017 letter, he described the experience in his own words:"When I started playing professionally at 17, my mother could barely watch because of the stress.""She would come to watch me play at the old Estadio José Alvalade, and she got so nervous during big games that she passed out a few times. Seriously, she passed out. The doctors started prescribing her sedatives just for my matches.""I would say to her, "Remember when you didn't care about football?" ;-)"The account offered a rare glimpse into the emotional side of Ronaldo's early success. While supporters watched a young talent take his first steps towards greatness, his mother experienced every important moment with overwhelming anxiety.Cristiano Ronaldo later stopped his mother from watching big gamesThe story did not end with his teenage years. In a 2019 interview with Piers Morgan, Ronaldo explained that he had eventually taken steps to protect his mother from the stress of watching him compete.He revealed that he no longer allowed her to attend major matches, including semi-finals and finals. Friends would stay with her or take her for walks while he played.Ronaldo also explained the personal reason behind that decision. After losing his father, José Dinis Aveiro, in 2005, he did not want to risk losing his mother too.The admission showed a different side of the football superstar. He had faced some of the world's best defenders without hesitation, but watching his mother struggle with the pressure of his career had been difficult.For Maria Dolores, every major match had carried an emotional weight that went far beyond the result. And for Ronaldo, protecting her had become more important than having her watch another big night in his football journey.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Can Mauricio Pochettino save Man United from Premier League relegation?
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of Manchester United for the first time on Sunday, in a trip to rivals Liverpool.
articles.body:
Manchester United will be led by a third manager in three years when Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first match since replacing Michael Carrick .

The fact that the Premier League clash is against their fierce rivals Liverpool – the team that, with United, are joint record English top-flight champions – is an added twist to a sordid recent tale for the Manchester club.

When Sir Alex Ferguson retired after lifting a then-record 20th league title in 2013, the Red Devils had climbed to the biggest and richest club in the world.

Now, apart from not being able to claim a Premier League crown since 2013, they are laden with debt – and worse still, they sit inside the relegation zone.

Can Pochettino save Man United from relegation?

The last time United were relegated from the top flight was in the 1973–1974 season. That came only six years after one of the club’s greatest nights – the lifting of the European Cup (now the Champions League), making them the first English club to do so.

Their fall this time around has not come quite as quickly, with their last crowning as European champions in 2008, and they have not been relegated – yet.

Few expect them to be. It would be unthinkable given the changed landscape of the entire footballing world, which has become awash with finances that clearly separate the elite and their resources from the rest.

When Pochettino was introduced to the media for the first time on Friday, the gathered press did not mention the word “relegation” even once.

So the simple answer is: yes, he can save the club from relegation. The longer equation is that the alternative would surely be the greatest shock in the history of a game famed for upsets and underdogs.

What problem does Pochettino need to solve first at United?

Words like identity, fitness, formation, and one that Pochettino awkwardly dropped on Friday, “philosophy”, have dogged every manager at Old Trafford since Ferguson’s departure.

“We arrived with the idea to create something from scratch, with our own philosophy and how we like to work,” Pochettino told the gathered reporters.

“We need to improve our players, find a way to perform, but the future and identity of the club is very clear.

“It is an historic club with an amazing years competing and being one of the best in the world.

“It is difficult to find another club that is the size of United. We need to be open-minded to do our best, and the players need to buy the idea that we need to improve.

“The job is to get the rest of the historic club, Manchester United, into a different place to where we are now.”

All of that can wait, because Liverpool are the next opponents, and for United, they do not come any bigger.

The Manchester derby has taken on a new level in recent years – although the tide there may also soon turn, depending on City’s appeal against their charges – but the rivalries against the Reds and Leeds United have the deepest roots for United fans.

A recent defeat to the revived latter still weighs heavily.

Pochettino needs to find a way for the team to start winning, and it needs to come soon. The club’s opening to the season is their worst since 1986, and one win – the worst return in the league – has left United just one point off bottom place.

By the time Pochettino and his United players walk out to the hostility of the Anfield crowd, they could be at the very foot of the table.

Will Pochettino change United’s formation?

The easiest part of the equation for Pochettino is the formation. With the United States national team, which he left to join United, the Argentinian deployed the 4-2-3-1 tactic that even Ferguson had evolved to in his final years.

Pochettino’s Tottenham, the club he made his managerial name with, were always set out in the same way with Harry Kane leading the line.

The United squad – which were moved to an uncomfortable 3-4-3 by Carrick’s predecessor, Ruben Amorim – are built for Pochettino’s style, but the task of melding them together had eluded Carrick and will be the key to their imminent return.

What long-term problems does Pochettino face at United?

The off-field troubles at United are well documented . The club are weighed down by the debts accrued with the Glazer family’s 2005 purchase.

Jim Ratcliffe’s investment three years ago has seen the Englishman and his INEOS group take control of footballing matters, but the annual interest the club pays remains a heavy burden.

The ownership is committed to its plan to rebuild the Old Trafford stadium to increase capacity and, with it, move the club to a more sustainable future.

That means the spending power that once saw United lead the way in transfer signings has diminished to the point where they cannot compete financially with Liverpool, City and Arsenal on the domestic front, let alone Spanish giants Real Madrid and Barcelona on the continent.

This is no easy fix for the manager or their owners, and is undoubtedly the long-term challenge for everyone involved.

What signings will Pochettino and United target in January transfer window?

Although the squad is set up for a 4-2-3-1 formation, they lack strength in depth.

Striker Benjamin Sesko has had an injury-plagued start to his United career since his move two seasons ago, and the Serbian international was far from the finished product when he arrived.

The 23-year-old’s absence this season has left a glaring hole up front, with Cameroon forward Bryan Mbeumo admirably leading the line with great endeavour, but lacking the presence a lone striker requires.

Despite needing a world-class finisher and being well stocked at the back, United have problems at the other end of the pitch, shipping 30 goals in all competitions this season.

Only two teams have conceded more than United’s 19 in the Premier League.

Luke Shaw’s availability at left-back has left United exposed in that position and made their failure to sign Lewis Hall in the summer all the more galling.

The Newcastle defender has since shone on international duty for England, and a move for the exciting 22-year-old in January seems the most obvious attempt United must make to appease their hugely unsettled fanbase.

What is Pochettino’s best Premier League finish?

Pochettino’s second-place finish with Tottenham in 2017 remains the North London club’s best league finish since 1962, only two years after their last top-flight title.

Will Pochettino be given enough time by United’s owners?

Pochettino will be the ninth manager to take charge of United in the last 13 seasons, and that does not include a further three interim coaches.

United fans never turn on their manager, and only recently, for the first time in the club’s history, have they turned on the players.

The same clearly cannot be said of the ownership.

It felt that Pochettino corrected his “philosophy” faux pas before he had finished that same answer on Friday. It was a word most associated with Louis van Gaal’s time at the club, and was rejected by players and fans alike.

United have an inbuilt philosophy and identity that buys players and managers time, built on attacking football and endless running.

The modern trend towards a high press should suit that mentality. To do that, Pochettino needs to unite the sleeping giants of Manchester. How long he will have to do so, based on the patience shown with his predecessors, is, however, anyone’s guess.

articles.title: Two Connecticut football products are making plays for first-place Central Connecticut State in the NEC
articles.summary: East Hartford's Dave Pardo and Bunnell product Mike Trovarelli are among the players helping CCSU lead the NEC.
articles.body:
NEW BRITAIN - Dave Pardo joked about having a fellow former Connecticut high school football product with the gift of grab in the Central Connecticut State receiver room even if Mike Trovarelli "comes from (203)."

Indeed, Trovarelli is a former Bunnell High standout and grew up in the heart of the portion of Connecticut that still utilizes the 203 area code. Pardo hails from East Hartford. That falls under the (860) area code for those following along.

Their paths never crossed during high school. However, this is their fourth season as teammates with the Blue Devils.

Pardo was the first to make an impact, making three catches in a win over Saint Francis in 2024. Trovarelli led the Blue Devils with 44 receptions and 493 receiving yards last season.

Pardo and Trovarelli each caught touchdown passes against Dartmouth and Sacred Heart during the 2025 season. They accomplished that feat once again in a recent 42-20 win over New Haven.

"Everybody can make a play and we trust each other to do that, so it is a real selfless act in practice and in games," Pardo said. "We just have to help each other because one of us is going to make a play."

Central Connecticut, the two-time defending Northeast Conference champion, dropped its first three games of the season. One loss came to Toledo, a title contender in the Mid-American Conference at the Football Bowl Subdivision level. That was followed by defeats to top-10 Football Championship Subdivision teams Montana State and South Dakota.

In the loss to Montana State, the reigning FCS champions, the Blue Devils found themselves an offensive bellcow in Davon Smith Jr. He ran for 92 yards as Central Connecticut pushed Montana State to the brink before falling 35-30.

He had 220 rushing yards against American International. Smith ran for 80 yards and a pair of touchdowns against New Haven.

CCSU has a top-25 rushing attack at the FCS level. That leaves fewer targets for a talented group of pass catchers.

Thirteen CCSU players have made at least two catches this season. Trovarelli leads the Blue Devils with 34 catches. He has a team-best five TD receptions and has averaged 14.54 yards per catch.

"Anybody can play, that is really good. It helps us during the game," Trovarelli said. "We trust each other and we have a bond with each other."

The Blue Devils are 16-3 in NEC play over the last three seasons. Pardo and Trovarelli are just two of the Connecticut products helping CCSU become the team to beat.

Jacob Staton and JJ Gibson, who both hail from Hamden, and Vernon's Malachi Mapp are among the top tacklers, Windsor's John Manning IV is the third-leading rusher, Jaden Langford of Windsor is another contributor on defense, while Newington's Nick Chomko and East Hartford's Thades Crump are starting offensive linemen.

"That is kind of the crux of our recruiting, local first and then we expand out," Central Connecticut State coach Adam Lechtenberg said. "Obviously family and friends can be here to watch them play and watch them support but guys like those two they have been great."

The Blue Devils are alone in first place in the NEC standings at 5-1 in conference play. There are three teams (Robert Morris, LIU and Duquesne) with two losses in league play. CCSU plays host to Duquesne at noon on Saturday at Arute Field.

A win and CCSU earns the NEC's FCS playoff berth. A loss and it would need an at-large berth

articles.title: No. 14 Oregon RB Dierre Hill limps off field with an injury in another hit for Ducks’ backfield
articles.summary: No. 14 Oregon has taken another hit in the backfield.
articles.body:
EAST LANSING, Mich. — No. 14 Oregon has taken another hit in the backfield.

Running back Dierre Hill limped off the field with an injury in the first quarter against Michigan State on Friday night.

Hill later went to the locker room, needing help and keeping weight off his left leg.

Jordon Davison , who has 439 yards rushing and a team-high seven touchdowns on the ground, missed his third straight game with a leg injury. Quarterback Dante Moore has not played since getting concussed on a late hit at Southern California in the fourth game of the season.

The banged-up Ducks are shooting to keep their chances alive for a spot in the 12-team playoff, entering the game No. 13 in the College Football Playoff rankings, with backups in key roles.

Brandon Smith , who was the third-string running back when Hill and Davison were healthy, broke a scoreless tie with a 5-yard touchdown run late in the first quarter against the Spartans.

Hill had four carries for 21 yards at Michigan State, giving him a team-high 593 yards rushing and five touchdowns this season. He has 25 receptions for 289 yards receiving and a 49-yard receiving touchdown.

Last year as a freshman, Hill ran for 656 yards and five touchdowns and had 16 catches for 137 yards and a score.

articles.title: Dylan Raiola, No. 13 Oregon Rout MSU Amid CFP Race, Top Box Score Player Stats & Highlights
articles.summary: The No. 13 Oregon Ducks kept their College Football Playoff hopes alive with a 45-7 victory over the Michigan State Spartans on Friday at Spartan Stadium.
articles.body:
The No. 13 Oregon Ducks kept their College Football Playoff hopes alive with a 45-7 victory over the Michigan State Spartans on Friday at Spartan Stadium.

Oregon has been on the bubble after losing three of its first seven games to start the season, but the Ducks have rapidly climbed the CFP rankings over the past two weeks.

Entering Friday's matchup, the Ducks had won three consecutive games while averaging more than 35 points per game during that span. Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola compiled 934 passing yards with nine touchdowns and no interceptions during that three-game win streak, and he was named Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week after throwing four touchdowns against Michigan last Saturday.

On Friday, Raiola took a backseat as Oregon's rushing attack and special teams dominated the Spartans. After the game which saw Oregon throwing late in the game with Raiola to extend its lead to 38, Ducks head coach Dan Lanning and Spartans head coach Pat Fitzgerald had a relatively lengthy exchange:

Here's a look at the top performers from both teams:

Oregon lost running back Dierre Hill Jr. to a leg injury early, but backups Brandon Smith and Simeon Price both scored two touchdowns. Smith opened the scoring by punching in a 5-yard touchdown run to give the Ducks a 7-0 lead in the first quarter.

Michigan State quarterback Kayd Coffman was unable to lead the Spartans to a first down on the team's first two possessions, but wide receiver Fredrick Moore kept his team's third possession alive with an impressive one-handed grab on a third-down play.

Although the Spartans outgained Oregon early, they ultimately had nothing to show for it. Michigan State missed a 46-yard field goal attempt, and Coffman tripped and fell on a failed fourth-down attempt. Then, a muffed punt gifted Oregon with another three points.

The Ducks drove down the field to end the second quarter with kicker Gage Hurych scoring a 15-yard touchdown on a fake field goal attempt. Oregon took a 17-0 lead into halftime.

Oregon extended its lead on the opening drive of the third quarter with running back Simeon Price capping off a 10-play, 65-yard drive.

The Spartans responded and scored their first touchdown on a 13-play, 47-yard drive, but it was too little, too late. Smith scored his second touchdown of the game to close out the third quarter on the following drive.

Oregon linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei intercepted Michigan State's freshman quarterback early in the fourth quarter, and Raiola connected with wide receiver Dakorien Moore on a 31-yard touchdown pass to give Oregon a 38-7 lead.

Oregon improved to an 8-3 record (6-2 Big Ten). The Ducks will undoubtedly continue their ascent up the rankings, but they'll have another must-win game against the Washington Huskies next Saturday. Michigan State is no longer eligible for a bowl game since the Spartans cannot reach the six-win threshold.

articles.title: Aimar Oroz: “Estoy con ganas de volver”
articles.standfirst: El mediapunta rojillo ya pone el foco en su vuelta a los terrenos de juego
articles.summary: El mediapunta rojillo ya pone el foco en su vuelta a los terrenos de juego
articles.body: Han pasado 81 días, una lesión, una recaída y un cambio de entrenador desde que Aimar Oroz jugó su último partido con Osasuna. Prácticamente tres meses en los cuales el conjunto rojillo ha echado de menos a su “10”, una sensación muy similar al anhelo del jugador de Arazuri por hacer lo que más le gusta: “Jugar al fútbol”. Aprovechando el evento de Kosner en Saltoki Home, el atacante habla con Marca sobre su recuperación y sus próximos objetivos con el cuadro navarro. Pregunta: Después de estos casi tres meses, la primera pregunta es clara: ¿Cómo estás? Respuesta: Se me ha hecho largo, pero ya estoy bien, entrenando con el equipo. Tengo muchas ganas y el domingo ya estoy de vuelta. P: Ya disponible en convocatoria, ¿también disponible para empezar de inicio? R: Yo he trabajado para estar perfectamente y me encuentro bien. Luego ya, el tiempo que pueda jugar el domingo no es decisión mía. P: Además del aspecto físico, las lesiones suelen afectar al factor psicológico. ¿Cómo lo has afrontado? R: La lesión la llevé bien, aunque la recaída me costó un poco más. Encima, pensaba que iba a ser menor el tiempo de baja y, al final, fue más. Sin embargo, me considero una persona bastante positiva y, aunque ha costado por esa recaída que coincidió con el final del parón largo, ya estoy con ganas de volver. P: ¿Cómo has vivido el cambio de dinámica e incluso de entrenador en este tiempo? R: Es cierto que ha cambiado un poco todo desde que estaba disponible. Estoy en el vestuario día a día y lo he vivido como cualquier otro compañero. El fútbol da muchas vueltas y ahora esperamos ir para arriba. P: ¿Cómo definirías la etapa de Luis Miguel Ramis en Osasuna? R: Diría que ha sido rara, empezamos bien y luego nos costó, aunque yo intento hacer lo mío lo mejor posible porque no soy yo quien toma las decisiones. P: ¿Por qué no cuajó su idea? R: No sé decirte exactamente qué no encajó, al principio no nos generaban mucho y luego empezamos a recibir unos cuantos goles. Quizá tampoco tuvimos esa suerte que hace falta a veces. P: Vuelve una cara muy conocida como la de Jagoba Arrasate, ¿has notado cambios con respecto a la anterior etapa? R: Conocemos muy bien tanto a Jagoba como a su cuerpo técnico. Seguro que ha vuelto con más experiencia, si cabe, y ha aprendido de su etapa fuera de Osasuna, pero no ha cambiado mucho. Se le ve ilusionado, y si estás así, normalmente suelen salir bien las cosas. P: Sobre el arranque de campaña, ¿cómo viviste el malestar en la grada o hecho de escuchar pitos en El Sadar? R: El final de temporada pasado fue muy duro para todos los rojillos y es normal que hubiera nervios al principio de temporada, cuando el equipo no acababa de arrancar. Es entendible, pero seguro que ahora vamos hacia arriba y la afición está siempre con nosotros, así que no les podemos decir nada. P: Del final de temporada, ¿qué sentiste en el último encuentro en el Coliseum? R: Mientras estás jugando es más tranquilo, ni generábamos ni nos generaban pero justo llegó su gol y se nos vino el mundo abajo. Por suerte, el Girona no consiguió ganar y nos quedamos en Primera. P: En cuanto a tus participaciones de gol, ¿te preocupa no tener cifras más altas? R: Tampoco me doy demasiada caña, pero estoy muy mentalizado con ello. Claramente quiero mejorar esos números y estoy seguro de que lo voy a hacer. P: Pese a ello, los resultados cuando no estás en el campo son mucho más negativos: ¿Qué aportas para que Osasuna sea mejor contigo? R: Supongo que también se habrá dado así por el factor de los partidos que me habré perdido. Quizá sume y ayude anímicamente, con ese punto de positivismo. P: Tu posición en el campo como mediapunta es clave. Igualmente, ¿te has planteado atrasar la posición para participar más en el juego? R: Siempre está esa opción y nos tenemos que adaptar a lo que nos toque. Igual luego juego ahí y no, pero creo que podría rendir bien en esa circunstancia y estar cómodo más atrás de lo que normalmente estoy. Aún así, de mediapunta estoy muy bien y creo que puedo aportar mucho al equipo así. P: Otros canteranos del equipo han mencionado la ilusión por ser capitán o un “One club man”, ¿qué piensas tú sobre esa posibilidad? R: Te diría que ni lo pienso. A mí me gusta el fútbol, disfruto jugando, voy día a día e intento mejorar cada día para intentar ganar cada partido. No pienso más allá de eso. P: Los próximos tres partidos son los peores clasificados de la tabla, ¿se está jugando el equipo una parte crucial de la temporada ahí? R: Cada partido te juegas mucho, pero es cierto que esos tres son rivales directos, por así decirlo. Tenemos que apretar desde ya para sacar puntos. P: ¿En qué posición tiene que quedar Osasuna para decir que se ha hecho una buena campaña? R: Del décimo hacia adelante.

articles.title: Un mes después vuelve otro Madrid
articles.standfirst: Los de Mou regresan al Bernabéu tras consolidar su gran momento en una gira triunfal con victorias a domicilio ante Barça, Racing, AEK y Valencia
articles.summary: Los de Mou regresan al Bernabéu tras consolidar su gran momento en una gira triunfal con victorias a domicilio ante Barça, Racing, AEK y Valencia
articles.body: Otro Real Madrid vuelve a casa un mes después. El equipo de Mourinho regresa al Bernabéu tras una gira triunfal de cuatro victorias a domicilio (Barcelona, Racing, AEK y Valencia) que le ha cambiado la cara por completo y lo ha catapultado tanto en Liga como en Champions. Los blancos hicieron las maletas tras ganar al Leipzig el 21 de octubre, en un momento en el que estaba a medio camino de la gran racha de ocho victorias consecutivas que protagonizan ahora mismo. Por entonces, el Real Madrid ganaba su cuarto partido seguido y se disponía a afrontar un tramo del calendario envenenado, con cuatro salidas de máxima exigencia que medían la reacción blanca. La primera prueba de fuego era ni más ni menos que el Camp Nou, superada con matrícula de honor. Un triunfo clave que impulsó a los de Mou en su pleno triunfal en el resto de los compromisos antes del nuevo parón. El Madrid salía súper reforzado de las cuatro finales lejos del Bernabéu y confirmaba su gran momento de forma y de resultados. Hoy el Bernabéu recibe a sus héroes con ganas de brindarles un cálido recibimiento tras meses de tira y afloja. La afición dará la bienvenida a un nuevo Madrid con el objetivo de formar una gran alianza con la que prolongar el gran momento del equipo. Porque tras cuatro partidos fuera, ahora llegan tres seguidos en casa (Celta, PSV y Alavés) para seguir dando rienda suelta a una racha de victorias de la que el equipo no disfrutaba desde hace bastante tiempo. “Llevamos mucho tiempo fuera del Bernabéu, es verdad, pero lo hemos hecho bien, hemos sacado todos los puntos que había que sacar. La gente está feliz de volver a estar junta, de volver a jugar en el Bernabéu y vamos a intentar empezar bien esta semana con tres partidos y sacar los puntos”, dijo Mourinho en la previa del regreso a la competición esta noche ante el Celta. Será el conjunto celeste el que intente fastidiar la fiesta de bienvenida del Bernabéu a un Madrid imparable desde el pasado 10 de octubre, cuando arrancó su gran racha actual con el triunfo ante el Villarreal. Desde entonces son más de 40 días en los que el equipo de blanco no para de ganar. Pero para Mou eso ya es pasado y piensa en lo que viene, que tampoco es fácil y que exigirá también el máximo del equipo, aún con muchos deberes pendientes. “Hay tres partidos en ocho días. Después llegan más. Terminamos un ciclo jugando contra el Arsenal y el partido del Arsenal será dos días después de jugar en Bilbao, y el de Bilbao será tres días después de jugar en San Sebastián. Es un calendario pesado, pero la gente quiere jugar. Ninguno de los internacionales se ha quedado fuera. Estamos todos”, dijo Mou.

articles.title: El récord del Cholo que puede durar muchas décadas
articles.standfirst: De ganar al Getafe será el entrenador con más partidos ganados en la historia de LaLiga.
articles.summary: De ganar al Getafe será el entrenador con más partidos ganados en la historia de LaLiga.
articles.body: Un triunfo, uno más, y Diego Pablo Simeone alcanzará las 345 victorias en LaLiga. Un triunfo, uno más, y nadie podrá mirar por el retrovisor al argentino en un récord que apunta a durar décadas. Un triunfo, uno más, y la leyenda de Luis se verá superada por aquel 14 de los 90 que arribó en 2011 con traje negro para elevar de dimensión al Atleti. En ella anda tres lustros después. El club que ‘decapitaba’ técnicos sin cesar, el que celebraba acabar cuarto para poder escuchar en vivo la música de la Champions, aquel Atlético que ha crecido de manera exponencial al ritmo del equipo del Cholo es el que debe decidir qué hacer con el futuro. Si será de la mano de quien cambió su historia. Si se echará en los brazos de otro. Faltan meses para que Simeone acabe su actual contrato. El ruido, el interesado de siempre, mueve el árbol por si cae alguna hoja. La realidad es que, salvo catástrofe, nadie imagina de momento un Atlético sin el Cholo. Los que mandan de verdad en los despachos llevan años teniéndolo claro: “No hay nadie mejor para el Atlético que Simeone, no hay mejor club para El Cholo que el Atlético”. Aten cabos.

articles.title: El mundo ya conoce a Tunkara: “Se lo debo todo a mi familia”
articles.standfirst: La Masia cuece un talento generacional: de jugar descalzo en Gambia a deslumbrar con España en el Mundial Sub-17
articles.summary: La Masia cuece un talento generacional: de jugar descalzo en Gambia a deslumbrar con España en el Mundial Sub-17
articles.body: Una de las últimas perlas nacidas de La Masia ya es más que una realidad. Un talento generacional que asoma con apenas 16 años. Una zurda capaz de todo. Un fútbol que seduce. Y una historia de superación que merece ser contada. Ebrima Tunkara se presentó al mundo. Lo hizo en Catar, en el escaparate de un Mundial Sub-17, con un golazo de falta y una asistencia extraordinaria para liderar la goleada de España ante China (5-0). La puesta de largo de un futbolista al que en Barcelona conocen bien. Al que Hansi Flick ya ha tenido a sus órdenes. Y que, mientras las miradas empiezan a dirigirse hacia él, tiene muy claro quiénes son los verdaderos protagonistas de su historia. "Mis familiares, que han estado ahí apoyándome desde el primer minuto. Les debo todo a ellos", confesó a MARCA tras el debut mundialista. Porque antes de Catar estuvo Gambia. Antes de La Masia, las calles de Lamoi. Y antes de las botas, los pies descalzos. Allí empezó todo. Entre partidos improvisados con sus amigos y una infancia humilde que el propio Tunkara recordó en una entrevista con la RFEF. "Jugábamos descalzos por la calle", relataba. Las porterías eran dos palos y para llegar al colegio debía recorrer varios kilómetros andando. Otra vida. Otra realidad. Hasta que su padre emprendió el camino hacia España en busca de un futuro mejor para los suyos. Ebrima tenía siete años cuando la familia pudo reunirse en Mataró. "Mi padre hizo un gran esfuerzo", reconoció tiempo después, tras regresar de vacaciones a su país natal y comprender mejor la dimensión de aquel sacrificio. En el barrio de Cerdanyola encontró su primer equipo. Un amigo de su padre lo animó a apuntarse y el talento hizo el resto. Pronto apareció el Barcelona, aunque el camino hacia La Masia tuvo un primer tropiezo. "Pensaba que era para ir al primer equipo", confesó a la RFEF sobre aquella primera llamada. La ingenuidad de un niño que todavía estaba descubriendo el fútbol de cantera. El estreno en las pruebas no salió como esperaba. El frío, el cambio de país y la adaptación a un nuevo entorno pesaban demasiado. Pero el Barça volvió a llamarlo. Una segunda oportunidad. Esta vez, sí. El pequeño que había aprendido a jugar descalzo en Gambia entraba en una de las fábricas de talento más prestigiosas del planeta. Su progresión ha sido vertiginosa. En enero de 2026 firmó su primer contrato profesional con el Barcelona y apenas unas semanas después debutó con el filial, todavía con 15 años. En verano llegó otro salto. Flick lo incorporó a la dinámica del primer equipo y Tunkara disputó sus primeros minutos en el amistoso ante el Birmingham City. De las calles de Lamoi a compartir entrenamientos con las estrellas del Barça. Todo antes de cumplir los 17. Zurdo, poderoso en la conducción y con una facilidad extraordinaria para encontrar espacios donde otros sólo ven piernas, el centrocampista tiene un espejo en el que mirarse. "El que más me gusta es Pedri", reconocía a la RFEF. Y su fútbol ya empieza a dejar huella. En el Europeo Sub-17 de Estonia fue elegido mejor jugador del torneo, después de repartir cuatro asistencias y acumular 23 pases clave. Y todo ha culminado en Catar. Su primer Mundial. Su primera gran exhibición. España dominaba a China, pero encontraba dificultades para derribar su entramado defensivo. Hasta que Pesquer abrió el marcador desde los once metros y Tunkara decidió que había llegado su momento. Provocó una falta cerca de la frontal y soltó un zurdazo imposible para el guardameta. Un misil que tenía su origen en Las Rozas. "Los pusimos a tirar dos días seguidos hasta reventarse las piernas", reveló David Cubillo. El propio futbolista confirmó a MARCA aquella preparación: "Estuvimos como dos o tres días lanzando faltas". Y todavía quedaba otra genialidad. En la segunda mitad recuperó el balón en campo propio, dejó atrás a tres rivales con una conducción eléctrica y regaló a Owen Emeka una asistencia para enmarcar. "Se siente muy bien, la verdad. Estoy muy orgulloso del partido que hemos hecho", reconoció con una sonrisa de oreja a oreja tras el encuentro. España acababa de endosar una manita a China y Tunkara había firmado una actuación que multiplicaba las expectativas alrededor de su figura. Pero entre tantos elogios, su pensamiento regresó a casa. A quienes hicieron posible el viaje desde Gambia y lo acompañaron durante sus primeros pasos en España. Preguntado por la primera persona a la que escribiría al llegar al vestuario, respondió sin dudar: "A mi padre, seguramente. Le diré que hemos ganado 5-0 y seguramente habrá visto el partido. Que esté orgulloso de mí". Y como en todas las historias, hay una promesa. Si España alcanza la final del Mundial, su padre viajará para acompañarlo. "Si llegamos, va a venir 100%", asegura. Todavía queda mucho camino hasta entonces. Para la selección y para un futbolista que apenas empieza a descubrir las exigencias de la élite. Porque los elogios no garantizan una carrera, ni siquiera cuando el talento parece desbordarse. Pero Tunkara ya ha recorrido un trayecto extraordinario. De Lamoi a Mataró. Del Cerdanyola a La Masia. De los entrenamientos con Flick a marcar en un Mundial. Y con una ambición que ya había confesado: "Quiero llegar a debutar con la Absoluta". El mundo empieza a conocer su nombre. Él no olvida de dónde viene. Ni a quién se lo debe.

articles.title: No. 13 Oregon uses special teams trickery again to ignite another runaway win, thumps Michigan State
articles.summary: Dan Lanning's aggression is paying dividends for the Ducks on their hunt for a College Football Playoff berth.
articles.body:
Long before No. 13 Oregon put the finishing touches on its 45-7 dismantling of Michigan State (3-8, 1-7 Big Ten) on Friday night in East Lansing, points were coming at a premium for the Ducks (8-3, 6-2).

For the second time in three games, head coach Dan Lanning used special teams trickery to ignite a runaway win.

With his team up 10-0 and seven seconds remaining in the second quarter, Lanning opted for a fake field goal on the final play of the first half. Instead of attempting a 33-yard attempt, kicker Gage Hurych received a pitch from his holder and, eventually, a block from tight end Jamari Johnson en route to the end zone.

Hurych broke one tackle and crossed the goal line prior to going down. Lanning was elated, as were his coaches and players.

The Ducks went on to score touchdowns on four of their first five drives of the second half. Their sixth and final series of the half consisted of a couple kneel downs.

"We just want to try to find every edge," Lanning said in his on-field postgame interview with Fox Sports.

"When there's an opportunity to create an edge, we want to be able to find it. Special teams have been game-changers for us this season. It's a great opportunity to create momentum. If we see it out there, we want to take advantage of it."

Oregon did the same thing at Ohio State on Nov. 7. At the time, the Ducks were trailing 14-3 to a No. 12 Buckeyes squad desperate for a bounce-back victory. Lanning was a facing a fourth-and-9 from his own 31-yard line.

He called for a fake punt that saw Teitum Tuioti catch the snap, run forward and then lob a jump pass to fellow outside linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei. The 6-foot-5, 265-pound Uiagalelei barreled down the sideline and capped a momentous 30-yard gain with a hurdle.

That drive ended in a touchdown and was a critical part of Oregon scoring 38 straight points in what wound up being a 41-28 win in Columbus .

Lanning's Ducks entered the season with the highest of expectations. Then their campaign for the program's first-ever national title went sideways. Quarterback Dante Moore suffered a scary concussion at USC . And the Ducks dropped two of their next three games and fell to 4-3 on the year.

Since, they've won four in a row. They're playing free, taking risks and having fun. Along the way, they've preserved their College Football Playoff hopes.

On Friday, Dylan Raiola — Moore's long-term replacement — threw for 234 yards and a touchdown, connecting with wide receiver Dakorien Moore for a highlight-reel 31-yard score in the fourth quarter. Moore deployed his right hand to reel in the end-zone shot.

The Ducks lost running back Dierre Hill Jr. to an apparent left leg injury early in the first quarter; however, Lanning told reporters afterward that he doesn't anticipate it being a "long-term injury."

The Ducks have one regular-season game left, and that's at home against rival Washington. It could very well be their final chance to leave it all out there, prove their worth to the CFP committee and maybe even showcase another special teams wrinkle.

articles.title: Jeers, injuries and doubters - Ben White's journey back to the top with England and Arsenal
articles.summary: When Ben White wheeled away after scoring England's third goal against world champions Spain, it was more than just a strike which ended up being the winner in a special win.
articles.body:
Ben White's crucial goal against world champions Spain on Sunday will not be forgotten by England fans for a long time.

A smart finish to cap a flowing Three Lions move gave Thomas Tuchel's men an almost unbelievable 3-0 lead in Madrid . They hung on - just - meaning White will always be remembered as the player who scored that winner.

But, for White, the moment represented more than just a goal. It signalled a dramatic turnaround in fortunes for his international career - just four years after many thought his England days were over.

The Arsenal defender has had a tough time on the international stage to say the least.

He left the World Cup in 2022 after a disagreement with then assistant manager Steve Holland and made himself unavailable during the rest of Gareth Southgate's time in charge.

Since returning to England duty in March under Tuchel, the 29-year-old has now established himself as arguably England's best right-back - despite facing jeers from sections of his own fans for his decision to leave that camp.

The defender, who initially arrived at Arsenal from Brighton as a centre-back, has had an excellent start to the season, having played a crucial part in the Gunners' first title win for 22 years last time out.

It hasn't been straightforward for him at Arsenal either though. White has had to navigate his own injury problems and at one point when the defender was struggling for fitness, there was talk that the Gunners should look at moving him on.

But White has battled back and even dealt with competition from Jurrien Timber to remain one of Arsenal 's key players.

People don't know full story behind England exile - White

60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages

"I think just obviously people don't know the full story, because I never said anything and won't put anyone under the bus", White said before the England win over Spain.

The 29-year-old is keen to put the well-covered departure from the World Cup in Qatar behind him.

After his long absence from playing for England, some supporters did not believe that White should return.

His first appearance at Wembley since that incident in a friendly against Uruguay in March was booed by some supporters, loud enough for Tuchel to be asked about it after the match.

That game in itself was dramatic for White, who scored the opening goal for England before giving away the penalty that saw the Three Lions draw 1-1 with Uruguay.

White, who missed the World Cup with injury, had been expecting the reaction from some fans. But he is used to proving himself and changing the perception around him.

Tuchel was keen to back his player and said in the build-up to the Spain game that he hoped that the chapter was closed on White being booed by his own supporters.

"Obviously a bit tricky and not straightforward, but yes, it's obviously amazing to be here now." White said of his return to England.

White said in that same interview that he would make the same decision again that he did at the World Cup, but it was now time to move on.

His displays show exactly where his mindset is for his country.

He played the final 12 minutes in England's win over Croatia at Wembley before being brought into the starting line-up for England's toughest match of the November international break against Spain.

This new era of England is being dubbed Tuchel 2.0 and White firmly seems to be part of it.

Chelsea defender Reece James is out with injury. He is a big favourite of Tuchel's but cannot be relied upon for every game due to injuries.

White is a key player for the Premier League champions, reliable in defence and a threat in attack while being physically imposing. There is a lot for Tuchel to like.

And with three of his Arsenal team-mates on the pitch as England won the game, and Bukayo Saka to return, White brings the positives of the cohesion of a club side to Tuchel's team.

Arsenal supporters not surprised by his performances

Arsenal supporters will not be surprised by White's excellent performances for England.

Since signing for the Gunners in 2021, not many players can say they have played more of a crucial role in Arsenal 's rebirth under Mikel Arteta.

Such is the importance of White, the Gunners attack does not flow as freely when he is not in the side to link up with Martin Odegaard and Saka as he relentlessly produces overlapping runs - a trait he showed when he scored England's third in Madrid.

His team-mates regularly say he is one of the fiercest competitors in training, and he has regularly shown his mentality when it looks as though things are going against him with his club side.

Arsenal signing Timber and a number of injury issues looked to have had White nearing an exit but, such is his determination, each time a challenge comes up he manages to turn it around.

White is a unique character within football, and has even said he doesn't watch the game away from the training ground, but his passion for his profession cannot be doubted.

Gunners fans will know that the level of passion he displayed in Madrid is something he shows every time he is on the pitch for his club side.
